                                                                          |                     |                  |\n\n## Repository files navigation\n\n* README\n* Code of conduct\n* MIT license\n  \n  \nVue Starport \n\nShared Vue component across routes with animations\n\nNPM version\n\nLive Demo\n\nEnglish | 简体中文\n  \n  \n\u003e **Note**: With the View Transitions API coming to the browsers, you may not this library anymore (even tho it's not a 1:1 replacement as View Transition does not preseve dom and state).\n\n## Why?\n\nIt's quite common you might have a same component used in different routes (pages) with a bit different sizes and positions. Sometimes you might want to animate them when user navigates between routes to provide a smooth UX. While such animation is common to be seen in native apps, it's could be a bit challenging to do it in Web.\n\nVue's component structure is presented as a **tree**, and the child components are in different branches with their own instances. Meaning when users navigate between routes, the components are not shared across routes.\n\nBy that means you can't directly animate the changes because they are in two different instances. The good news is, there is a technique called FLIP to enumerate the transitions between them.\n\nHowever, FLIP only solves the problem of transitions, the components are still not the same. During the navigation, the internal state of the component will lost.\n\nThus I started this new approach **Starport** to experiment with a better solution to fit this requirement.\n\n## How?\n\nSo since we can't share the components across different branches in the component tree, we could actually hoist them to the root so they become independent from the routes.\n\nTo allow each page to still have control of the components, we introduced a **Proxy component** to present the expected size and position of that component. The proxy will pass the props and position information to the actual component and let it \"fly over\" the proxy with animations.\n\nWhen the transition ends and it arrived to the expected position, it will then \"land down\" to the actual component using the \u003cTeleport/\u003e component.\n\nWith this \"landing\" mechanism, the DOM tree will be preserved as what you will have with the original tree structure. When navigating to another route, the component then will \"lift off\" back to the floating state, \"fly\" to the new proxy's position and \"land\" again.\n\nThis is very similar to Terran's Buildings in StarCraft (able to leave the ground and fly to new locations). It's also the inspiration source of the project name **Starport**.\n\n## Install\n\n\u003e ⚗️ **Experimental**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpm i vue-starport\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\u003e Vue Starport only works for Vue 3\n\n## Usage\n\nAdd &#96;\u003cStarportCarrier\u003e&#96; component from &#96;vue-starport&#96; to your root component (&#96;app.vue&#96;). All &#96;\u003cStarport\u003e&#96; usage should be inside &#96;\u003cStarportCarrier\u003e&#96; component.\n\n\u003cscript setup\u003e\nimport { StarportCarrier } from 'vue-starport'\n\u003c/script\u003e\n\n\u003ctemplate\u003e\n  \u003cStarportCarrier\u003e \u003c!-- here --\u003e\n    \u003cRouterView /\u003e\n  \u003c/StarportCarrier\u003e\n\u003c/template\u003e\n\nIn routes, wrap the component with the &#96;\u003cStarport\u003e&#96; component.\n\n\u003c!-- PageA.vue --\u003e\n\u003cscript setup\u003e\nimport { Starport } from 'vue-starport'\n\u003c/script\u003e\n\n\u003ctemplate\u003e\n  \u003cdiv\u003e\n    \u003c!-- ... --\u003e\n    \u003cStarport port=\"my-id\" style=\"height:400px\"\u003e \n      \u003cMyComponent :prop=\"value\"/\u003e\n    \u003c/Starport\u003e\n  \u003c/div\u003e\n\u003c/template\u003e\n\nOn the other page, we do the same thing with **the same &#96;port&#96; id** to identify the instance.\n\n\u003c!-- PageB.vue --\u003e\n\u003cscript setup\u003e\nimport { Starport } from 'vue-starport'\n\u003c/script\u003e\n\n\u003ctemplate\u003e\n  \u003cdiv\u003e\n    \u003c!-- ... --\u003e\n    \u003cStarport port=\"my-id\" style=\"height:600px\"\u003e\n      \u003cMyComponent :prop=\"value\"/\u003e\n    \u003c/Starport\u003e\n  \u003c/div\u003e\n\u003c/template\u003e\n\n\u003e Note that you might need to apply some styles to &#96;\u003cStarport\u003e&#96; to make it have a defined size indicating the area for the \"floating starcraft\" to land.\n\nCheckout the Playground for more examples.\n\n### Register Components Globally\n\n// main.ts\nimport StarportPlugin from 'vue-starport'\n\napp.use(StarportPlugin())\n\nAnd then you can use &#96;Starport&#96; and &#96;StarportCarrier&#96; components without importing.\n\n### Keep Alive\n\nBy default, when navigating to a page without a corresponding &#96;\u003cStarport\u003e&#96; proxy to land, the component will be destroyed. If you want to keep the component alive even when it's not presented in the current route, you can set &#96;keepAlive&#96; to &#96;true&#96; for that specific instance.\n\n\u003cStarport keep-alive port=\"my-id\"\u003e\n  \u003cMyComponent /\u003e\n\u003c/Starport\u003e\n\nTo configure it globally, you can pass options to the plugin:\n\n// main.ts\nimport StarportPlugin from 'vue-starport'\n\napp.use(StarportPlugin({ keepAlive: true }))\n\n## Debug\n\nTo debug what happens during the transition, you can add the follow CSS to highlight the parts\n\n[data-starport-craft] {\n  background: #0805;\n}\n[data-starport-proxy]:not([data-starport-landed]) {\n  background: #8005;\n}\n\n## Special Thanks\n\nThanks to @hangsman who helped to provide the initial solution of proper teleport the element and made this idea valid. Also thanks to the viewers of my live-streaming on Bilibili, those who spend time with me to working on this idea and provided useful feedback during the live.\n\nYou can check the recordings of my live-streams (in Chinese), where I wrote this project from scratch.\n\n你可以在哔哩哔哩观看我实现此项目的 直播录像。\n\n## Sponsors\n\n## License\n\nMIT License © 2022 Anthony Fu\n\n## About\n\n 🛰 Shared component across routes with animations\n\nvue-starport.netlify.app/ \n\n### Resources\n\n Readme \n\n### License\n\n MIT license \n\n### Code of conduct\n\n Code of conduct \n\nActivity \n\n### Stars\n\n**1.9k** stars \n\n### Watchers\n\n**8** watching \n\n### Forks\n\n**98** forks \n\n Report repository \n\n## Releases2\n\nv0.4.0  Latest Sep 7, 2023 \n\n\\+ 1 release\n\n## Sponsor this project\n\n Sponsor \n\nLearn more about GitHub Sponsors \n\n## Contributors13\n\n## Languages\n\n* TypeScript 67.1%\n* Vue 23.8%\n* JavaScript 5.4%\n* HTML 2.1%\n* CSS 1.6%\n\n## Footer\n\n © 2025 GitHub, Inc. \n\n### Footer navigation\n\n* Terms\n* Privacy\n* Security\n* Status\n* Docs\n* Contact\n* Manage cookies\n* Do not share my personal information\n\n You can’t perform that action at this time.",

Thanks.  \n– wdtj  \nCommented Sep 4, 2020 at 13:18\n\nAdd a comment  | \n\n9 \n\n# Addendum - git version 2.34.1.windows.1 \u0026 others(?)\n\nRegrettably, &#96;git config core.protectNTFS false&#96; turned out not to be enough; **the contents of the colon-carrying filenames are lost (filesize = 0)**.\n\n## Solution\n\n### TL;DR\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ngit diff ec28c8ddd5f8c83d11604bcae69afb46d79b1029 \u003e p.patch\npatch -R -f -i p.patch\ngit add *\ngit commit \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Elaboration\n\nTurns out &#96;git config core.protectNTFS false&#96; does work, insofar as to **not produce fatal errors on &#96;git checkout&#96; anymore**.\n\nHowever, git now will produce filenames _clipped_ to the colon and with **zero content**.\n\nE.g. &#96;Writing-Bops:-The-Bebop-Schema-Language.md&#96; (\\~9KB) --\u003e &#96;Writing-Bops&#96; (0 KB)\n\nTo fix this, we need to get a copy of the original offending file(s)' content another way, so we can restore it.\n\n\u003e ### Conditions / Assumptions\n\u003e \n\u003e * This assumes you _cannot_ or _will not_ use a _sparse_ clone for some reason.\n\u003e * Ditto on &#96;git apply-filter&#96; and other techniques to 'permanently rewrite' git history, f.e. when you are tracking a third-party git repo.\n\u003e * You're running Windows, using NTFS storage, git-for-windows with &#96;bash&#96; as your shell and have a &#96;patch.exe&#96; available (&#96;patch --version&#96; should report something like \"GNU patch 2.7.6\")\n\n(_In our case, we were messing about with a github wiki clone and ran into this issue of filenames containing colons. Of course, we wanted to fix this in place, without going the extra 'sparse clone' or WSL mile._)\n\nTurns out we can get the missing content after we did\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ngit config core.protectNTFS false\ngit checkout \u003chash\u003e\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nby running &#96;patch&#96;. (BTW: TortoiseGit would _hang forever_ if you tried to diff/compare these commits!)\n\nUse this next command to get a patch file with all the missing changes. If you have multiple files with colons or other trouble, _all_ the missing content will be listed in the patchfile: one patchfile to catch it all!\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ngit diff ec28c8ddd5f8c83d11604bcae69afb46d79b1029 \u003e p.patch\n# ^^^^ reference the git hash with the offending original file(s)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNow that you have a patchfile, you can apply it to the current _working directory_: it must be applied _in reverse_ (&#96;-R&#96;):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\npatch -R -f -i p.patch\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIf you forget &#96;-R&#96;, patch will ask (answer &#96;[y]es&#96;); if you _do_ specify &#96;-R&#96; patch will yak even more, so &#96;-f&#96; (_force_) is in order to shut up patch and just do the job.\n\nThis should list one or more files being patched as a result, e.g.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n$ patch -R -f -i p.patch\npatching file Writing-Bops:-The-Bebop-Schema-Language.md\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\u003e **Note the colon in that filename**: turns out GNU patch on windows (at least v2.7.6) uses a _Unicode homoglyph_ to **simulate** a colon in a filename. See also further below.\n\nYou now have the original content of the colon-ed files in your _working directory_ and you're now ready to add these files to the git index and commit them as usual:\n\n\u003e **Warning:** you'll probably need to cleanup (delete) the empty _clipped_ filenames produced by your earlier &#96;git checkout&#96; before proceeding!\n\n\u003e **Note:** if you don't like the homoglyphed filename &#96;patch -i&#96; assigned to the missing content, you can change it to anything you like before committing the result.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ngit add *\ngit commit \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Verifying results\n\nWhen you did everything right, that last commit should list the colon-ed file as **renamed** as you did not change the content and &#96;git commit&#96; should thus have detected the \"file rename action\" as-is.\n\n## Extra: replacing colon with a _homoglyph_\n\nI found several Unicode homoglyphs that look more or less like a colon, but are considered _legal_ in NTFS filenames.\n\nAfter a bit of experimentation, I decided on using &#96;꞉&#96; as I wanted to keep the github wiki page I was fiddling with intact as much as possible.\n\nGenerally, I would discard the colon entirely, or replace it with one or more hyphens, but in the case of wiki MarkDown pages, that decision can go the other way.\n\nShare \n\nImprove this answer \n\n Follow \n\n answered Dec 17, 2021 at 17:18 \n\nGer Hobbelt's user avatar \n\nGer HobbeltGer Hobbelt \n\n1,21811 gold badge1313 silver badges1818 bronze badges \n\nAdd a comment  | \n\n5 \n\nI discovered one option that had not been mentioned. Use WSL to checkout the files.\n\nI ran &#96;git clone&#96; in WSL/Bash instead of PowerShell/CMD. WSL handles fixing the filenames transparently, even though they are still stored on NTFS and I open them using VS Code for Windows. I was able to modify the files in Windows, and push my changes on Windows even.\n\nShare \n\nImprove this answer \n\n Follow \n\n answered Dec 9, 2021 at 22:02 \n\npseudosavant's user avatar \n\npseudosavantpseudosavant \n\n7,27422 gold badges4141 silver badges4343 bronze badges \n\nAdd a comment  | \n\n5 \n\nIn GitHub: Going to the Repo URL (\u003chttps://github.com/UserNameHere/RepoNameHere\u003e), then Clicking \"Code\" \u003e \"Download ZIP\" and then extracting the .zip file in Windows was successful for me (I had to skip invalid files)\n\nenter image description here\n\nenter image description here\n\nShare \n\nImprove this answer \n\n Follow \n\n answered Mar 12, 2022 at 15:04 \n\nJesus is Lord's user avatar \n\nJesus is LordJesus is Lord \n\n15.4k1111 gold badges6969 silver badges101101 bronze badges \n\n1 \n\n* 1  \nConfirming that when download as a Zip, 7-zip renames all folders named aux \\_aux  \n– Code Whisperer  \nCommented Nov 11, 2022 at 17:39\n\nAdd a comment  | \n\n4 \n\nbefore using &#96;git clone&#96;\n\nexecute this command:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ngit config --global core.protectNTFS false\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nShare \n\nImprove this answer \n\n Follow \n\n answered Nov 2, 2021 at 19:43 \n\nedocollado's user avatar \n\nedocolladoedocollado \n\n62977 silver badges99 bronze badges \n\n1 \n\n* 10  \nAbsolutely do not do this. navigation\n\n* README\n* GPL-3.0 license\n\n# Marker\n\nMarker converts documents to markdown, JSON, and HTML quickly and accurately.\n\n* Converts PDF, image, PPTX, DOCX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB files in all languages\n* Formats tables, forms, equations, inline math, links, references, and code blocks\n* Extracts and saves images\n* Removes headers/footers/other artifacts\n* Extensible with your own formatting and logic\n* Optionally boost accuracy with LLMs\n* Works on GPU, CPU, or MPS\n\n## Performance\n\nMarker benchmarks favorably compared to cloud services like Llamaparse and Mathpix, as well as other open source tools.\n\nThe above results are running single PDF pages serially. Marker is significantly faster when running in batch mode, with a projected throughput of 122 pages/second on an H100 (.18 seconds per page across 22 processes).\n\nSee below for detailed speed and accuracy benchmarks, and instructions on how to run your own benchmarks.\n\n## Hybrid Mode\n\nFor the highest accuracy, pass the &#96;--use_llm&#96; flag to use an LLM alongside marker. This will do things like merge tables across pages, handle inline math, format tables properly, and extract values from forms. It can use any gemini or ollama model. By default, it uses &#96;gemini-2.0-flash&#96;. See below for details.\n\nHere is a table benchmark comparing marker, gemini flash alone, and marker with use\\_llm:\n\nAs you can see, the use\\_llm mode offers higher accuracy than marker or gemini alone.\n\n## Examples\n\n| PDF                                                                   | File type   | Markdown                                                                                                                  | JSON                                                                                              |\n| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| [Think Python](https://greenteapress.com/thinkpython/thinkpython.pdf) | Textbook    | [View](https://github.com/VikParuchuri/marker/blob/master/data/examples/markdown/thinkpython/thinkpython.md)              | [View](https://github.com/VikParuchuri/marker/blob/master/data/examples/json/thinkpython.json)    |\n| [Switch Transformers](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2101.03961.pdf)           | arXiv paper | [View](https://github.com/VikParuchuri/marker/blob/master/data/examples/markdown/switch%5Ftransformers/switch%5Ftrans.md) | [View](https://github.com/VikParuchuri/marker/blob/master/data/examples/json/switch%5Ftrans.json) |\n| [Multi-column CNN](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1804.07821.pdf)              | arXiv paper | [View](https://github.com/VikParuchuri/marker/blob/master/data/examples/markdown/multicolcnn/multicolcnn.md)              | [View](https://github.com/VikParuchuri/marker/blob/master/data/examples/json/multicolcnn.json)    |\n\n# Commercial usage\n\nI want marker to be as widely accessible as possible, while still funding my development/training costs. Research and personal usage is always okay, but there are some restrictions on commercial usage.\n\nThe weights for the models are licensed &#96;cc-by-nc-sa-4.0&#96;, but I will waive that for any organization under $5M USD in gross revenue in the most recent 12-month period AND under $5M in lifetime VC/angel funding raised. You also must not be competitive with the Datalab API. If you want to remove the GPL license requirements (dual-license) and/or use the weights commercially over the revenue limit, check out the options here.\n\n# Hosted API\n\nThere's a hosted API for marker available here:\n\n* Supports PDFs, word documents, and powerpoints\n* 1/4th the price of leading cloud-based competitors\n* High uptime (99.99%), quality, and speed (around 15 seconds to convert a 250 page PDF)\n\n# Community\n\nDiscord is where we discuss future development.\n\n# Installation\n\nYou'll need python 3.10+ and PyTorch. You may need to install the CPU version of torch first if you're not using a Mac or a GPU machine. See here for more details.\n\nInstall with:\n\npip install marker-pdf\n\nIf you want to use marker on documents other than PDFs, you will need to install additional dependencies with:\n\npip install marker-pdf[full]\n\n# Usage\n\nFirst, some configuration:\n\n* Your torch device will be automatically detected, but you can override this. For example, &#96;TORCH_DEVICE=cuda&#96;.\n* Some PDFs, even digital ones, have bad text in them. Set the &#96;force_ocr&#96; flag to ensure your PDF runs through OCR, or the &#96;strip_existing_ocr&#96; to keep all digital text, and strip out any existing OCR text.\n\n## Interactive App\n\nI've included a streamlit app that lets you interactively try marker with some basic options. Run it with:\n\npip install streamlit\nmarker_gui\n\n## Convert a single file\n\nmarker_single /path/to/file.pdf\n\nYou can pass in PDFs or images.\n\nOptions:\n\n* &#96;--output_dir PATH&#96;: Directory where output files will be saved. Defaults to the value specified in settings.OUTPUT\\_DIR.\n* &#96;--output_format [markdown|json|html]&#96;: Specify the format for the output results.\n* &#96;--paginate_output&#96;: Paginates the output, using &#96;\\n\\n{PAGE_NUMBER}&#96; followed by &#96;-&#96; \\* 48, then &#96;\\n\\n&#96;\n* &#96;--use_llm&#96;: Uses an LLM to improve accuracy. You must set your Gemini API key using the &#96;GOOGLE_API_KEY&#96; env var.\n* &#96;--redo_inline_math&#96;: If you want the highest quality inline math conversion, use this along with &#96;--use_llm&#96;.\n* &#96;--disable_image_extraction&#96;: Don't extract images from the PDF. If you also specify &#96;--use_llm&#96;, then images will be replaced with a description.\n* &#96;--page_range TEXT&#96;: Specify which pages to process. Accepts comma-separated page numbers and ranges. Example: &#96;--page_range \"0,5-10,20\"&#96; will process pages 0, 5 through 10, and page 20.\n* &#96;--force_ocr&#96;: Force OCR processing on the entire document, even for pages that might contain extractable text.\n* &#96;--strip_existing_ocr&#96;: Remove all existing OCR text in the document and re-OCR with surya.\n* &#96;--debug&#96;: Enable debug mode for additional logging and diagnostic information.\n* &#96;--processors TEXT&#96;: Override the default processors by providing their full module paths, separated by commas. Example: &#96;--processors \"module1.processor1,module2.processor2\"&#96;\n* &#96;--config_json PATH&#96;: Path to a JSON configuration file containing additional settings.\n* &#96;--languages TEXT&#96;: Optionally specify which languages to use for OCR processing. Accepts a comma-separated list. Example: &#96;--languages \"en,fr,de\"&#96; for English, French, and German.\n* &#96;config --help&#96;: List all available builders, processors, and converters, and their associated configuration. These values can be used to build a JSON configuration file for additional tweaking of marker defaults.\n* &#96;--converter_cls&#96;: One of &#96;marker.converters.pdf.PdfConverter&#96; (default) or &#96;marker.converters.table.TableConverter&#96;. The &#96;PdfConverter&#96; will convert the whole PDF, the &#96;TableConverter&#96; will only extract and convert tables.\n* &#96;--llm_service&#96;: Which llm service to use if &#96;--use_llm&#96; is passed. This defaults to &#96;marker.services.gemini.GoogleGeminiService&#96;.\n* &#96;--help&#96;: see all of the flags that can be passed into marker. (it supports many more options then are listed above)\n\nThe list of supported languages for surya OCR is here. If you don't need OCR, marker can work with any language.\n\n## Convert multiple files\n\nmarker /path/to/input/folder --workers 4\n\n* &#96;marker&#96; supports all the same options from &#96;marker_single&#96; above.\n* &#96;--workers&#96; is the number of conversion workers to run simultaneously. This is set to 5 by default, but you can increase it to increase throughput, at the cost of more CPU/GPU usage. Marker will use 5GB of VRAM per worker at the peak, and 3.5GB average.\n\n## Convert multiple files on multiple GPUs\n\nNUM_DEVICES=4 NUM_WORKERS=15 marker_chunk_convert ../pdf_in ../md_out\n\n* &#96;NUM_DEVICES&#96; is the number of GPUs to use. Should be &#96;2&#96; or greater.\n* &#96;NUM_WORKERS&#96; is the number of parallel processes to run on each GPU.\n\n## Use from python\n\nSee the &#96;PdfConverter&#96; class at &#96;marker/converters/pdf.py&#96; function for additional arguments that can be passed.\n\nfrom marker.converters.pdf import PdfConverter\nfrom marker.models import create_model_dict\nfrom marker.output import text_from_rendered\n\nconverter = PdfConverter(\n    artifact_dict=create_model_dict(),\n)\nrendered = converter(\"FILEPATH\")\ntext, _, images = text_from_rendered(rendered)\n\n&#96;rendered&#96; will be a pydantic basemodel with different properties depending on the output type requested. With markdown output (default), you'll have the properties &#96;markdown&#96;, &#96;metadata&#96;, and &#96;images&#96;. For json output, you'll have &#96;children&#96;, &#96;block_type&#96;, and &#96;metadata&#96;.\n\n### Custom configuration\n\nYou can pass configuration using the &#96;ConfigParser&#96;. To see all available options, do &#96;marker_single --help&#96;.\n\nfrom marker.converters.pdf import PdfConverter\nfrom marker.models import create_model_dict\nfrom marker.config.parser import ConfigParser\n\nconfig = {\n    \"output_format\": \"json\",\n    \"ADDITIONAL_KEY\": \"VALUE\"\n}\nconfig_parser = ConfigParser(config)\n\nconverter = PdfConverter(\n    config=config_parser.generate_config_dict(),\n    artifact_dict=create_model_dict(),\n    processor_list=config_parser.get_processors(),\n    renderer=config_parser.get_renderer(),\n    llm_service=config_parser.get_llm_service()\n)\nrendered = converter(\"FILEPATH\")\n\n### Extract blocks\n\nEach document consists of one or more pages. Pages contain blocks, which can themselves contain other blocks. It's possible to programmatically manipulate these blocks.\n\nHere's an example of extracting all forms from a document:\n\nfrom marker.converters.pdf import PdfConverter\nfrom marker.models import create_model_dict\nfrom marker.schema import BlockTypes\n\nconverter = PdfConverter(\n    artifact_dict=create_model_dict(),\n)\ndocument = converter.build_document(\"FILEPATH\")\nforms = document.contained_blocks((BlockTypes.Form,))\n\nLook at the processors for more examples of extracting and manipulating blocks.\n\n## Other converters\n\nYou can also use other converters that define different conversion pipelines:\n\n### Extract tables\n\nThe &#96;TableConverter&#96; will only convert and extract tables:\n\nfrom marker.converters.table import TableConverter\nfrom marker.models import create_model_dict\nfrom marker.output import text_from_rendered\n\nconverter = TableConverter(\n    artifact_dict=create_model_dict(),\n)\nrendered = converter(\"FILEPATH\")\ntext, _, images = text_from_rendered(rendered)\n\nThis takes all the same configuration as the PdfConverter. You can specify the configuration &#96;force_layout_block=Table&#96; to avoid layout detection and instead assume every page is a table. Set &#96;output_format=json&#96; to also get cell bounding boxes.\n\nYou can also run this via the CLI with\n\nmarker_single FILENAME --use_llm --force_layout_block Table --converter_cls marker.converters.table.TableConverter --output_format json\n\n# Output Formats\n\n## Markdown\n\nMarkdown output will include:\n\n* image links (images will be saved in the same folder)\n* formatted tables\n* embedded LaTeX equations (fenced with &#96;$$&#96;)\n* Code is fenced with triple backticks\n* Superscripts for footnotes\n\n## HTML\n\nHTML output is similar to markdown output:\n\n* Images are included via &#96;img&#96; tags\n* equations are fenced with &#96;\u003cmath\u003e&#96; tags\n* code is in &#96;pre&#96; tags\n\n## JSON\n\nJSON output will be organized in a tree-like structure, with the leaf nodes being blocks. Examples of leaf nodes are a single list item, a paragraph of text, or an image.\n\nThe output will be a list, with each list item representing a page. Each page is considered a block in the internal marker schema. There are different types of blocks to represent different elements.\n\nPages have the keys:\n\n* &#96;id&#96; \\- unique id for the block.\n* &#96;block_type&#96; \\- the type of block. The possible block types can be seen in &#96;marker/schema/__init__.py&#96;. As of this writing, they are \\[\"Line\", \"Span\", \"FigureGroup\", \"TableGroup\", \"ListGroup\", \"PictureGroup\", \"Page\", \"Caption\", \"Code\", \"Figure\", \"Footnote\", \"Form\", \"Equation\", \"Handwriting\", \"TextInlineMath\", \"ListItem\", \"PageFooter\", \"PageHeader\", \"Picture\", \"SectionHeader\", \"Table\", \"Text\", \"TableOfContents\", \"Document\"\\]\n* &#96;html&#96; \\- the HTML for the page. Note that this will have recursive references to children. The &#96;content-ref&#96; tags must be replaced with the child content if you want the full html. You can see an example of this at &#96;marker/output.py:json_to_html&#96;. That function will take in a single block from the json output, and turn it into HTML.\n* &#96;polygon&#96; \\- the 4-corner polygon of the page, in (x1,y1), (x2,y2), (x3, y3), (x4, y4) format. (x1,y1) is the top left, and coordinates go clockwise.\n* &#96;children&#96; \\- the child blocks.\n\nThe child blocks have two additional keys:\n\n* &#96;section_hierarchy&#96; \\- indicates the sections that the block is part of. &#96;1&#96; indicates an h1 tag, &#96;2&#96; an h2, and so on.\n* &#96;images&#96; \\- base64 encoded images. The key will be the block id, and the data will be the encoded image.\n\nNote that child blocks of pages can have their own children as well (a tree structure).\n\n{\n      \"id\": \"/page/10/Page/366\",\n      \"block_type\": \"Page\",\n      \"html\": \"\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/SectionHeader/0'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/SectionHeader/1'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/Text/2'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/Text/3'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/Figure/4'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/SectionHeader/5'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/SectionHeader/6'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/TextInlineMath/7'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/TextInlineMath/8'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/Table/9'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/SectionHeader/10'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\u003ccontent-ref src='/page/10/Text/11'\u003e\u003c/content-ref\u003e\",\n      \"polygon\": [[0.0, 0.0], [612.0, 0.0], [612.0, 792.0], [0.0, 792.0]],\n      \"children\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"/page/10/SectionHeader/0\",\n          \"block_type\": \"SectionHeader\",\n          \"html\": \"\u003ch1\u003eSupplementary Material for \u003ci\u003eSubspace Adversarial Training\u003c/i\u003e \u003c/h1\u003e\",\n          \"polygon\": [\n            [217.845703125, 80.630859375], [374.73046875, 80.630859375],\n            [374.73046875, 107.0],\n            [217.845703125, 107.0]\n          ],\n          \"children\": null,\n          \"section_hierarchy\": {\n            \"1\": \"/page/10/SectionHeader/1\"\n          },\n          \"images\": {}\n        },\n        ...\n        ]\n    }\n\n## Metadata\n\nAll output formats will return a metadata dictionary, with the following fields:\n\n{\n    \"table_of_contents\": [\n      {\n        \"title\": \"Introduction\",\n        \"heading_level\": 1,\n        \"page_id\": 0,\n        \"polygon\": [...]\n      }\n    ], // computed PDF table of contents\n    \"page_stats\": [\n      {\n        \"page_id\":  0, \n        \"text_extraction_method\": \"pdftext\",\n        \"block_counts\": [(\"Span\", 200), ...]\n      },\n      ...\n    ]\n}\n\n# LLM Services\n\nWhen running with the &#96;--use_llm&#96; flag, you have a choice of services you can use:\n\n* &#96;Gemini&#96; \\- this will use the Gemini developer API by default. You'll need to pass &#96;--gemini_api_key&#96; to configuration.\n* &#96;Google Vertex&#96; \\- this will use vertex, which can be more reliable. You'll need to pass &#96;--vertex_project_id&#96;. To use it, set &#96;--llm_service=marker.services.vertex.GoogleVertexService&#96;.\n* &#96;Ollama&#96; \\- this will use local models. You can configure &#96;--ollama_base_url&#96; and &#96;--ollama_model&#96;. To use it, set &#96;--llm_service=marker.services.ollama.OllamaService&#96;.\n* &#96;Claude&#96; \\- this will use the anthropic API. You can configure &#96;--claude_api_key&#96;, and &#96;--claude_model_name&#96;. To use it, set &#96;--llm_service=marker.services.claude.ClaudeService&#96;.\n* &#96;OpenAI&#96; \\- this supports any openai-like endpoint. You can configure &#96;--openai_api_key&#96;, &#96;--openai_model&#96;, and &#96;--openai_base_url&#96;. To use it, set &#96;--llm_service=marker.services.openai.OpenAIService&#96;.\n\nThese services may have additional optional configuration as well - you can see it by viewing the classes.\n\n# Internals\n\nMarker is easy to extend. The core units of marker are:\n\n* &#96;Providers&#96;, at &#96;marker/providers&#96;. These provide information from a source file, like a PDF.\n* &#96;Builders&#96;, at &#96;marker/builders&#96;. These generate the initial document blocks and fill in text, using info from the providers.\n* &#96;Processors&#96;, at &#96;marker/processors&#96;. These process specific blocks, for example the table formatter is a processor.\n* &#96;Renderers&#96;, at &#96;marker/renderers&#96;. These use the blocks to render output.\n* &#96;Schema&#96;, at &#96;marker/schema&#96;. The classes for all the block types.\n* &#96;Converters&#96;, at &#96;marker/converters&#96;. They run the whole end to end pipeline.\n\nTo customize processing behavior, override the &#96;processors&#96;. To add new output formats, write a new &#96;renderer&#96;. For additional input formats, write a new &#96;provider.&#96;\n\nProcessors and renderers can be directly passed into the base &#96;PDFConverter&#96;, so you can specify your own custom processing easily.\n\n## API server\n\nThere is a very simple API server you can run like this:\n\npip install -U uvicorn fastapi python-multipart\nmarker_server --port 8001\n\nThis will start a fastapi server that you can access at &#96;localhost:8001&#96;. You can go to &#96;localhost:8001/docs&#96; to see the endpoint options.\n\nYou can send requests like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport requests\nimport json\n\npost_data = {\n    'filepath': 'FILEPATH',\n    # Add other params here\n}\n\nrequests.post(\"http://localhost:8001/marker\", data=json.dumps(post_data)).json()\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote that this is not a very robust API, and is only intended for small-scale use. If you want to use this server, but want a more robust conversion option, you can use the hosted Datalab API.\n\n# Troubleshooting\n\nThere are some settings that you may find useful if things aren't working the way you expect:\n\n* If you have issues with accuracy, try setting &#96;--use_llm&#96; to use an LLM to improve quality. You must set &#96;GOOGLE_API_KEY&#96; to a Gemini API key for this to work.\n* Make sure to set &#96;force_ocr&#96; if you see garbled text - this will re-OCR the document.\n* &#96;TORCH_DEVICE&#96; \\- set this to force marker to use a given torch device for inference.\n* If you're getting out of memory errors, decrease worker count. You can also try splitting up long PDFs into multiple files.\n\n## Debugging\n\nPass the &#96;debug&#96; option to activate debug mode. This will save images of each page with detected layout and text, as well as output a json file with additional bounding box information.\n\n# Benchmarks\n\n## Overall PDF Conversion\n\nWe created a benchmark set by extracting single PDF pages from common crawl. We scored based on a heuristic that aligns text with ground truth text segments, and an LLM as a judge scoring method.\n\n| Method     | Avg Time | Heuristic Score | LLM Score |\n| ---------- | -------- | --------------- | --------- |\n| marker     | 2.83837  | 95.6709         | 4.23916   |\n| llamaparse | 23.348   | 84.2442         | 3.97619   |\n| mathpix    | 6.36223  | 86.4281         | 4.15626   |\n| docling    | 3.69949  | 86.7073         | 3.70429   |\n\nBenchmarks were run on an H100 for markjer and docling - llamaparse and mathpix used their cloud services. We can also look at it by document type:\n\n| Document Type        | Marker heuristic | Marker LLM | Llamaparse Heuristic | Llamaparse LLM | Mathpix Heuristic | Mathpix LLM | Docling Heuristic | Docling LLM |\n| -------------------- | ---------------- | ---------- | -------------------- | -------------- | ----------------- | ----------- | ----------------- | ----------- |\n| Scientific paper     | 96.6737          | 4.34899    | 87.1651              | 3.96421        | 91.2267           | 4.46861     | 92.135            | 3.72422     |\n| Book page            | 97.1846          | 4.16168 98.4021          | 4.5        | 93.4477              | 4.28125        | 96.0383           | 4.45312     | 92.0952           | 4.09375     |\n| Engineering document | 93.9244          | 4.04412    | 77.4854              | 3.72059        | 80.3319           | 3.88235     | 79.6807           | 3.42647     |\n| Legal document       | 96.689           | 4.27759    | 86.9769              | 3.87584  |\n\n## Throughput\n\nWe benchmarked throughput using a single long PDF.\n\n| Method | Time per page | Time per document | VRAM used |\n| ------ | ------------- | ----------------- | --------- |\n| marker | 0.18          | 43.42             | 3.17GB    |\n\nThe projected throughput is 122 pages per second on an H100 - we can run 22 individual processes given the VRAM used.\n\n## Table Conversion\n\nMarker can extract tables from PDFs using &#96;marker.converters.table.TableConverter&#96;. The table extraction performance is measured by comparing the extracted HTML representation of tables against the original HTML representations using the test split of FinTabNet. The HTML representations are compared using a tree edit distance based metric to judge both structure and content. Marker detects and identifies the structure of all tables in a PDF page and achieves these scores:\n\n| Method            | Avg score | Total tables |\n| ----------------- | --------- | ------------ |\n| marker            | 0.816     | 99           |\n| marker w/use\\_llm | 0.907     | 99           |\n| gemini            | 0.829     | 99           |\n\nThe &#96;--use_llm&#96; flag can significantly improve table recognition performance, as you can see.\n\nWe filter out tables that we cannot align with the ground truth, since fintabnet and our layout model have slightly different detection methods (this results in some tables being split/merged).\n\n## Running your own benchmarks\n\nYou can benchmark the performance of marker on your machine. Install marker manually with:\n\ngit clone https://github.com/VikParuchuri/marker.git\npoetry install\n\n### Overall PDF Conversion\n\nDownload the benchmark data here and unzip. Then run the overall benchmark like this:\n\npython benchmarks/overall.py --methods marker --scores heuristic,llm\n\nOptions:\n\n* &#96;--use_llm&#96; use an llm to improve the marker results.\n* &#96;--max_rows&#96; how many rows to process for the benchmark.\n* &#96;--methods&#96; can be &#96;llamaparse&#96;, &#96;mathpix&#96;, &#96;docling&#96;, &#96;marker&#96;. Comma separated.\n* &#96;--scores&#96; which scoring functions to use, can be &#96;llm&#96;, &#96;heuristic&#96;. Comma separated.\n\n### Table Conversion\n\nThe processed FinTabNet dataset is hosted here and is automatically downloaded. Run the benchmark with:\n\npython benchmarks/table/table.py --max_rows 100\n\nOptions:\n\n* &#96;--use_llm&#96; uses an llm with marker to improve accuracy.\n* &#96;--use_gemini&#96; also benchmarks gemini 2.0 flash.\n\n# How it works\n\nMarker is a pipeline of deep learning models:\n\n* Extract text, OCR if necessary (heuristics, surya)\n* Detect page layout and find reading order (surya)\n* Clean and format each block (heuristics, texify, surya)\n* Optionally use an LLM to improve quality\n* Combine blocks and postprocess complete text\n\nIt only uses models where necessary, which improves speed and accuracy.\n\n# Limitations\n\nPDF is a tricky format, so marker will not always work perfectly. Here are some known limitations that are on the roadmap to address:\n\n* Very complex layouts, with nested tables and forms, may not work\n* Forms may not be rendered well\n\nNote: Passing the &#96;--use_llm&#96; flag will mostly solve these issues.\n\n# Thanks\n\nThis work would not have been possible without amazing open source models and datasets, including (but not limited to):\n\n* Surya\n* Texify\n* Pypdfium2/pdfium\n* DocLayNet from IBM\n\nThank you to the authors of these models and datasets for making them available to the community!\n\n## About\n\n Convert PDF to markdown + JSON quickly with high accuracy\n\nwww.datalab.to \n\n### Resources\n\n Readme \n\n### License\n\n GPL-3.0 license \n\nActivity \n\n### Stars\n\n**24.7k** stars \n\n### Watchers\n\n**96** watching \n\n### Forks\n\n**1.6k** forks \n\n Report repository \n\n## Releases52\n\nBugfixes  Latest Mar 26, 2025 \n\n\\+ 51 releases\n\n## Packages0\n\n No packages published   \n\n## Contributors17\n\n* @VikParuchuri\n* @iammosespaulr\n* @tarun-menta\n* @github-actions[bot]\n* @conjuncts\n* @jazzido\n* @samuell\n* @denisshepelin\n* @tagliala\n* @syldor\n* @xiaoyao9184\n* @tosaddler\n* @tjbck\n* @dantetemplar\n\n\\+ 3 contributors\n\n## Languages\n\n* Python 97.9%\n* HTML 1.7%\n* Shell 0.4%\n\n## Footer\n\n © 2025 GitHub, Inc. \n\n### Footer navigation\n\n* Terms\n* Privacy\n* Security\n* Status\n* Docs\n* Contact\n* Manage cookies\n* Do not share my personal information\n\n You can’t perform that action at this time.",

(leave empty if unsure) App directory (appDir: true) Link to the code that reproduces this issue \u003chttps://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/stupefied-browser-tlwo8y?file=%2FREADME.md\u003e To Reproduce I provided a larger repro for context, as it is unclear which combination of factors leads to the specific bug, although a number of other people report [the same issue](https://github.com/framer/motion/issues/1850). Describe the Bug Framer Motion supports a feature called shared layout animation that automatically transitions components whose styles have changed when the container (that contains them) re-renders. This feature appears not to be working in multiple scenarios with Next.js 13 under the app folder. In the provided example, this feature is applied to the blue navigation highlight. The affected container in the code sandbox is: \u003chttps://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/stupefied-browser-tlwo8y?file=%2Flib%2Fcomponents%2FNavigation.tsx\u003e To produce the undesired behavior, I simply applied layoutId as specified in the [relevant Framer Motion documentation](https://www.framer.com/motion/guide-upgrade/#shared-layout-animations) to the motion elements expected to transition. Framer Motion 5 removes the AnimateSharedLayout component.Now, you can use the layoutId prop and components will animate from one to another without the need for the AnimateSharedLayout wrapper. I believe I also tried more explicit variations. Others have reported similar or identical issues in the [bug currently open](https://github.com/framer/motion/issues/1850) with Framer Motion. Expected Behavior I expect the blue highlight to slide smoothly to its new position when the nav container re-renders. Which browser are you using? (if relevant) Version 113.0.5672.63 (Official Build) (64-bit) How are you deploying your application? (if relevant) Usually Vercel [NEXT-1151](https://linear.app/vercel/issue/NEXT-1151/app-router-issue-with-framer-motion-shared-layout-animations) |\n| 13motiondivision/motion#1850 \n\n Closed \n\n@joshdavenport \n\n Copy link \n\n### \n\n**joshdavenport**  commentedMay 5, 2023 • \n\n edited \n\nLoading \n\n| As an extra point for this issue, [the docs specify that using templates is a way to achieve enter/exit animations](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts#templates) ([web archive link](https://web.archive.org/web/20230818163342/https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts#templates), see edit) with either CSS or an animation library (for which framer-motion would be one of the go-to choices for most I feel) but doesn't offer any indication as to how to achieve this. With templates, even if you wrap children in layout (where templates is rendered, and even given a key) transitions just don't work because there's no way to make that template a framer motion element with animate props. **Edit:** This wording is now removed, just linking the docs as they were at this moment in time so it doesn't look like I was saying the docs say something it doesn't: [web archive link](https://web.archive.org/web/20230818163342/https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts#templates) |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n\n👍 1 madfcat reacted with thumbs up emoji \n\nAll reactions \n* 👍 1 reaction\n\n Sorry, something went wrong.\n\n@zackdotcomputer \n\n Copy link \n\nContributor \n\n### \n\n**zackdotcomputer**  commentedMay 10, 2023 \n\n| I believe I've pinpointed the issue that is causing this problem. As part of the new app router structure, Next lays out a tree of components that includes the following loop (rendering a hypothetical /path/subpath request): \\- Root Layout   \\- OuterLayoutRouter     \\- TemplateContext.Provider key=\"path\"       \\- Root Template         \\- InnerLayoutRouter           \\- Path Layout             \\- OuterLayoutRouter               \\- TemplateContext.Provider key=\"subpath\"                 \\- Path Template (not subpath, as that is a page.tsx)                   \\- InnerLayoutRouter                     \\- OuterLayoutRouter                       \\- TemplateContext.Provider key=\"\\_\\_PAGE\\_\\_\"                         \\- Page contents Crucially, the app framework is inserting an OuterLayoutRouter component between each Layout and corresponding Template. This component is what is responsible for performing the content swap when the user navigates to a new path. The system seems to select the lowest OuterLayoutRouter that can be used (e.g. for the path navigation /sign-up/step1 to /sign-up/step2 the second OuterLayoutRouter, which represents the directory /sign-up and lives inside any layout.tsx for that directory, would be used. If the paths were /sign-up/step/1 to /sign-up/step/2, then the third OuterLayoutRouter would be used. And so on...). Because the OuterLayoutRouter fully swaps its contents to the new path, and because those contents include the template.tsx, the template cannot provide an \"on exit\" effect (as it will have been pruned from the tree already). Because the OuterLayoutRouter itself does not have a key (because it is not swapped), the layout cannot include an AnimatePresence because that component requires its **direct child** have a key that indicates navigation. Finally, because the usePathname function only updates after the render swap has been performed, one cannot sneak a key into the stack. If one tries to hack in an exit-enter effect by making a layout that uses the pathname to indicate when its child has changed, then the contents will be swapped to the new page and then fade-out and fade-back-in. The potential fixes I see for this issue are: Next's render stack could be changed so that the Layout and Template are rendered in an immediate parent/child relationship, which TBH is [what the documentation says should happen](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts#templates) (I'll open a separate bug for this) Next could expose an API or event that indicates when a navigation begins and what the destination path is, so that one could add a key to the layout when loading begins. I don't think there is a way with the APIs currently exposed to solve this issue on Framer's side without at least some change from Next. |\n| Then we can have more fine grained control over when things are re-mounted. As an example right now two different pages that return the same component in the same position will get remounted: // app/foo/page.js export default function Page() {   return \u003cCounter /\u003e; } // app/bar/page.js export default function Page() {   return \u003cCounter /\u003e; } These two counter's state will be lost when soft-navigating between /foo and /bar. By removing the key props from the tree that Next builds, we can decide ourselves if we want to remount things: // app/foo/page.js export default function Page() {   const pathname \\= usePathname();   return \u003cCounter key\\={pathname} /\u003e; // \u003c-- don't preserve the counter state on soft-navigations } This would of course allow us to properly adjust exit-animations, as well as other more fine-grained things we want to happen when soft-navigating. |\n| \n\n**cutsoy**  commentedAug 11, 2023 • \n\n edited \n\nLoading \n\n| The workaround I'm using memorizes the LayoutRouterContext (using useRef) and passes its down to its children. This ensures that the old route doesn't get unmounted on navigation. Full example below: /// layout.tsx function FrozenRouter(props: PropsWithChildren\u003c{}\\\u003e) {     const context \\= useContext(LayoutRouterContext);     const frozen \\= useRef(context).current;     return (         \u003cLayoutRouterContext.Provider value\\={frozen}\\\u003e             {props.children}         \u003c/LayoutRouterContext.Provider\\\u003e     ); } export default function Layout(props: PropsWithChildren\u003c{}\\\u003e) {     const pathname \\= usePathname();          return \u003cAnimatePresence\\\u003e         \u003cmotion.div             key\\={pathname}             initial\\={{ opacity: 0 }}             animate\\={{ opacity: 0 }}             exit\\={{ opacity: 0 }}             transition\\={{ duration: 0.4, type: \"tween\" }}         \\\u003e             \u003cFrozenRouter\\\u003e{props.children}\u003c/FrozenRouter\\\u003e         \u003c/motion.div\\\u003e     \u003c/AnimatePresence\\\u003e; } This is working pretty good so far. Here was my use case: I needed to animate between different routes, from / to an individual product page The URL should update when changing routes, and both clicking back in the navbar and the browser back button need to work Reloading the page on the product detail page /p/\\[slug\\] needs to correctly start on the detail state (no animation) I can definitely empathize with this being confusing, and apologize we haven't done enough to create examples or show how this could be possible. For example, trying to animate across routes using framer-motion (now motion) using the default page files in the App Router won't work exactly – you can't use the layoutId to transition the element. You might think – okay, maybe I need to use intercepted routes for a modal-like pattern, but that also isn't the right solution here. The solution I landed on is this: I'm using motion to animate between my two different \"states\" in the app (grid of products, product detail page) When clicking on a product, we start the animation but also [shallow update](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/linking-and-navigating#windowhistorypushstate) the URL with window.history.pushState We add a useEffect to listen to the popstate event to handle the browser back action We have a /p/\\[slug\\]/page.tsx route, which has the detail page, to handle direct linking or reloads post-animation This isn't perfect – for example, if you manually swipe back in iOS Safari. The most ideal solution here is View Transitions, which you can use \u003chttps://next-view-transitions.vercel.app\u003e for in some cases. However, I couldn't get it working perfectly for the animation I was going for in this case, and also there isn't [Firefox support](https://caniuse.com/view-transitions) yet for View Transitions. I do believe this is the best solution in the future though. Code: \u003chttps://github.com/leerob/next-minimal-store\u003e Demo: \u003chttps://nextzy.vercel.app/\u003e CleanShot.2024-12-29.at.14.56.21.mp4 Hope this helps! 🙏 |\n| Just use next-view-transitions: .overlay {position: fixed;z-index: 100;top: 0;left: 0;width: 100vw;height: 100vh;background: var(--dark) ;clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 100% 100%, 100% 100%, 0 100%);pointer-events: auto;view-transition-name: overlay;} [@Keyframes](https://github.com/Keyframes) slide-out {from {background: var(--dark) ;\\-webkit-clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 100% 100%, 100% 100%, 0 100%);clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 100% 100%, 100% 100%, 0 100%);}to {background: var(--dark) ;clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 100% 100%, 100% 0, 0 0);}} [@Keyframes](https://github.com/Keyframes) slide in {from {background: var(--dark) ;clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 100% 100%, 100% 0, 0 0); }to {background: var(--dark) ;clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 0, 0 0);}} ::view-transition-old(overlay) {animation: slide out 0.8s ease ; } ::view-transition-new(overlay) {animation: slide-in 1s ease ;animation delay: 0.8s;} am satisfied |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n\n👎 4 rogit31, ryparker, thiagorossener, and lousb reacted with thumbs down emoji \n\nAll reactions \n* 👎 4 reactions\n\n Sorry, something went wrong.\n\n@S-Sim0n \n\n Copy link \n\n### \n\n**S-Sim0n**  commentedMar 8, 2025 \n\n| Forgot the most important thing to keep the old page simple works with browser arrows as well as with links: /\\* Fade-Out für die alte Seite (root) \\*/::view-transition-old(root) {animation: fade-out 0.8s linear; } /\\* Fade-In für die neue Seite (root) \\*/::view-transition-new(root) {animation: fade-in 0.8s linear; /\\* Wartet, bis fade-out fertig ist \\*/} [@Keyframes](https://github.com/Keyframes) fade-out {from {opacity: 1;}to {opacity: 0.999;}} [@Keyframes](https://github.com/Keyframes) fade-in {from {opacity: 0;}to {opacity: 0;}} .overlay {position: fixed;z-index: 100;top: 0;left: 0;width: 100vw;height: 100vh;background: var(--dark) ;clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 100% 100%, 100% 100%, 0 100%);pointer-events: auto;view-transition-name: overlay;} [@Keyframes](https://github.com/Keyframes) slide-out {from {background: var(--dark) ;\\-webkit-clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 100% 100%, 100% 100%, 0 100%);clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 100% 100%, 100% 100%, 0 100%);}to {background: var(--dark) ;clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 100% 100%, 100% 0, 0 0);}} [@Keyframes](https://github.com/Keyframes) slide-in {from {background: var(--dark) ;clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 100% 100%, 100% 0, 0 0); }to {background: var(--dark) ;clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 0, 0 0);}} ::view-transition-old(overlay) {animation: slide-out 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.2, 0.25, 1); } ::view-transition-new(overlay) {animation: slide-in 1s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.2, 0.25, 1);animation-delay: 0.8s;} |\n| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n\n👎 3 thiagorossener, victorpavlenko, and lousb reacted with thumbs down emoji \n\nAll reactions \n* 👎 3 reactions\n\n Sorry, something went wrong.\n\nSign up for free **to join this conversation on GitHub**. As a simplified example you can pass environment variables to client components via server components: // .env SPECIAL\\_TOKEN\\=\"abc123\" // src/components/Example.client.tsx export const Example \\= ({token}: {token: string}) \\=\u003e {   return (     \u003cdiv\\\u003e       \u003cp\\\u003e{token}\u003c/p\\\u003e     \u003c/div\\\u003e   ); }; // src/routes/index.server.tsx import {Example} from '\\~/components'; function HomepageContent() {   return (     \u003cExample token\\={Oxygen.env.SPECIAL\\_TOKEN} /\\\u003e   ) } Would that kind of pattern work for you? It's important from a security perspective that runtime variables aren't exposed to the client automatically because that could give bad actors access to data that they shouldn't have (e.g. private/secret tokens). The Problem Say I have two sibling CRA apps, Foo and Bar. What is the best practice for sharing a common component, Baz between the two apps? Scope It would make sense to have a sibling folder Baz with it's own package.json, and to use npm link to access it from Foo and Bar. But it seems that [npm link has bigger issues](https://github.com/npm/npm/issues/10343), so maybe we should explore alternatives. One example is [wml](https://github.com/wix/wml), which simply watches and copies files. Building Even when npm link works fine, the JSX in Baz has not been compiled. Per [this discussion](https://github.com/facebookincubator/create-react-app/issues/1125), I think we should compile separate modules like Baz independently, but that will require boilerplate such as babel config. CRA helps avoid this for full apps, but we don't yet have create-react-component to help manage the boilerplate of shared components. Optimizing for Developer Experience There are a few ways to clean this up, but I'm curious what people think is the current best practice. What is the ideal developer experience? |\n| reactions \n\n Sorry, something went wrong.\n\n@ericvicenti \n\n Copy link \n\nAuthor \n\n### \n\n**ericvicenti**  commentedFeb 7, 2017 \n\n| Ok, [@gaearon](https://github.com/gaearon), based on your previous comments, it seems that this issue is pretty ripe for fixing. RFC of a cohesive solution Please poke this proposal full of holes 😄 Part I: The new meta Creator We may want to give people more tools like CRA in the future, but it isn't desirable to force people to install a new global dependency for each tool. Instead, I'd like to propose one tool to rule them all: create-react: npm install -g create-react # This is equivalent to \\&#96;create-react-app MyApp\\&#96; create-react app MyApp # Now we can support: create-react component Foo Behind the scenes, this tool will look up the latest npm package to do the heavy lifting. For example, create-react app actually is implemented by the react-creator-app package. The react-creator-component package would define the behavior of create-react component. This opens up more innovation in the space, because a random company could publish react-creator-mycompany-project, and everybody can easily try out their environment by running create-react mycompany-project. Also, this could replace react-native init, which could become create-react mobile, create-react native or something. Part II: The Component Dev Setup One of the new creators would be the 'component' creator, which creates a new React component package. Like a CRA app, it includes scripts as devDependencies, and has local commands like npm run build, which builds using the standard Babel configuration. It would output whatever module standard is expected by standard CRA apps. One major difference is that npm start will build the component and watch for changes, rather than launching a server. At this point, developers could use npm start alongside [linklocal](https://www.npmjs.com/package/linklocal) to hack on their components from a neighboring react app. One huge argument for doing this is to improve tooling for React Native components. Currently, most RN libraries publish uncompiled code, which has become a nightmare when attempting to share libraries or components in other environments that expect node\\_modules to be compiled. By introducing a common set of library scripts, we can build a comfortable path forward to compiled modules. Part III: Improve experience within an app The only bad part about the above experience is the manual usage of linklocal and the npm start for each component you may want to hack on. In the future, the react-scripts of CRA could be upgraded to automatically run linklocal, so that changes made in neighboring modules are immediately reflected in the development app. Then, react-scripts can detect when an app's linked component is supported by the same scripts, and can automatically run the watch-and-build behavior for each of the compatible components. So, if I had Foo and Bar as independent apps that each depended on a sibling Baz component, I could run either app and still see the updates as I make changes to Baz. Thoughts? Let me ping a few more smart people who have a lot of context on this: [@cpojer](https://github.com/cpojer) [@thejameskyle](https://github.com/thejameskyle) [@skevy](https://github.com/skevy) [@taion](https://github.com/taion) [@ljharb](https://github.com/ljharb) I'm excited to work on this because I've felt this pain a lot- especially when trying to share code between React Native and web/CRA. Please let me know if you think this makes sense! I'm happy to put together a prototype, if people like this approach. |\n| Assume you have 3 React apps: A reusable component as a standalone React app. Let's call it GoodComponent. We keep it as a standalone app since we want to use it in multiple apps. Its name in package.json is **good-component**. **Assume the main file of this GoodComponent is src/index.js**. An actual React application called FooApp. Another React application called BarApp. cd to root directory of GoodComponent npm linkcd to root directory of FooApp npm link good-componentcd to root directory of BarApp npm link good-componentIn the code of FooApp or BarApp, if you want to use GoodComponnet, you can just import it as below: import GoodComponent from 'good-component/src' Here we go! You can now have your own temporary npm module. You can reuse it just as an npm module without publishing it. |\n| Ask questions, find answers and collaborate at work with Stack Overflow for Teams.Explore Teams\n\n##### Collectives™ on Stack Overflow\n\nFind centralized, trusted content and collaborate around the technologies you use most.\n\n Learn more about Collectives \n\n**Teams**\n\nQ\u0026A for work\n\nConnect and share knowledge within a single location that is structured and easy to search.\n\n Learn more about Teams \n\n# How to pass environment variable received from GitHub actions\n\n Ask Question \n\nAsked 5 years, 7 months ago \n\nModified 1 year, 9 months ago \n\nViewed 40k times\n\n Part of CI/CD Collective\n\n19 \n\nIn my action.yml I defined an input:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nname: 'test action'\nauthor: Param Thakkar\ndescription: 'test'\n\ninputs: \n  test_var:\n    description: 'A test variable'\n    required: true\n\nruns:\n  using: 'docker'\n  image: 'Dockerfile'\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAnd in my workflow I passed the test\\_var:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nname: CI\n\non: [push]\n\njobs:\n  build:\n\nruns-on: ubuntu-latest\n\nsteps:\n  - name: Test the GH action\n    uses: paramt/github-actions-playground@master\n    with:\n      test_var: \"this is just a test\"\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSo there should be an environment variable that's created when the workflow runs, right? But when I run this short python script:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport os\n\nprint(os.getenv('TEST_VAR'))\nprint(\"It works!\")\n\nexit(0)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIt prints:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nNone\nIt works!\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nI think that I have to pass the ENV variable through my Dockerfile... Right now my Dockerfile looks like this: \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nFROM python:latest\n\n# Add files to the image\nADD entrypoint.py /entrypoint.py\nADD requirements.txt /requirements.txt\n\n# Save ENV var in a temp file\nRUN $TEST_VAR \u003e /temp_var\n\n# Install dependencies and make script executable\nRUN pip install -r requirements.txt\nRUN chmod +x entrypoint.py\n\nRUN echo \"temp var: \"\nRUN cat /temp_var\n\n# Run script with the ENV var\nENTRYPOINT export TEST_VAR=\"$TEST_VAR\"; /entrypoint.py\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBut the variable isn't echoed and isn't passed to the pythons script either.. am I missing something? When I tried to set my &#96;$TEMP_VAR&#96; to a random piece of string, it _is_ sent through to the Python script. Is this a mistake on my behalf or is the GitHub action not working as intended?\n\nHere's the link to the test repo\n\n* docker\n* dockerfile\n* github-actions\n\nShare \n\nImprove this question \n\n Follow \n\n asked Oct 4, 2019 at 19:43 \n\nParam's user avatar \n\nParamParam \n\n72922 gold badges66 silver badges1616 bronze badges \n\n1 \n\n* How were you able to access your input arg defined in action.yml inside your Dockerfile? I'm trying to do the same and I'm having some trouble with that.  \n– jidicula  \nCommented Jan 19, 2021 at 1:24\n\nAdd a comment  | \n\n##  4 Answers4 \n\n Sorted by:  Reset to default \n\n Highest score (default)  Trending (recent votes count more)  Date modified (newest first)  Date created (oldest first) \n\n13 \n\nI think you are trying to read the wrong environment variable name. GitHub Actions adds &#96;INPUT_&#96; to the name of the input variable. So try the following:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nprint(os.getenv('INPUT_TEST_VAR'))\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nFrom the documentation:\n\n\u003e When you specify an input to an action in a workflow file or use a default input value, GitHub creates an environment variable for the input with the name INPUT\\_. The environment variable created converts input names to uppercase letters and replaces spaces with \\_ characters.\n\u003e \n\u003e For example, if a workflow defined the numOctocats and octocatEyeColor inputs, the action code could read the values of the inputs using the INPUT\\_NUMOCTOCATS and INPUT\\_OCTOCATEYECOLOR environment variables.\n\n\u003chttps://help.github.com/en/articles/metadata-syntax-for-github-actions#inputs\u003e\n\nShare \n\nImprove this answer \n\n Follow \n\n answered Oct 4, 2019 at 22:56 \n\npeterevans's user avatar \n\npeterevanspeterevans \n\n42.6k1010 gold badges9494 silver badges8989 bronze badges \n\nAdd a comment  | \n\n9 \n\nA bit late but for the next one, you can also use the &#96;env&#96; field :\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nname: CI\n\non: [push]\n\njobs:\n  build:\n\nruns-on: ubuntu-latest\n\nsteps:\n  - name: Test the GH action\n    uses: paramt/github-actions-playground@master\n    env:\n      test_var: \"this is just a test\"\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nwhich will be included during the creation of your docker and pass without the prefix &#96;INPUT_&#96;\n\nShare \n\nImprove this answer \n\n Follow \n\nedited Aug 28, 2020 at 9:53 \n\n answered Aug 28, 2020 at 9:30 \n\nQuentin's user avatar \n\nQuentinQuentin \n\n35933 silver badges1414 bronze badges \n\n1 \n\n* 3  \ndoes that make it available inside the container or does that require another step?  \n– rob  \nCommented Nov 30, 2022 at 12:04\n\nAdd a comment  | \n\n5 \n\nKeep env vars secret by specifying them in &#96;Settings -\u003e Secrets&#96; in the repo, and then calling them in the workflow:\n\nFor example, consider a workflow that runs an &#96;R&#96; script followed by a &#96;Python&#96; script. First, in &#96;.github/workflows/my_job.yml&#96; notice the &#96;MY_VAR&#96; variable, which points to a stored secret with &#96;${{ secrets.MY_VAR}}&#96;. The rest is standard code (run on cron, specify Ubuntu OS and Docker image, define workflow steps).\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\non:\n  schedule:\n    - cron:  '0 17 * * *'\njobs:\n  my_job:\n    name: my job\n    env:\n      MY_VAR: ${{ secrets.MY_VAR }}\n    runs-on: ubuntu-18.04\n    container:\n     image: docker.io/my_username/my_image:my_tag\n    steps:\n      - name: checkout_repo\n        uses: actions/checkout@v2\n      - name: run some code\n        run: bash ./src/run.sh \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNext, in the scripts that compose your workflow, you can access the env var specified in the workflow file above as you would locally.\n\nFor example, in the repo, let's assume &#96;src/run.sh&#96; calls an &#96;R&#96; script followed by a &#96;Python&#96; script.\n\nIn &#96;R&#96; access the env var and store as an object:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmy_var \u003c- Sys.getenv(\"MY_VAR\")\n\n.\n.\n.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn &#96;Python&#96; access the env var and store as an object:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport os\n\nmy_var = os.getenv(\"MY_VAR\")\n.\n.\n.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSee the docs here.\n\nShare \n\nImprove this answer \n\n Follow \n\nedited Feb 8, 2022 at 16:13 \n\n answered Oct 25, 2021 at 0:59 \n\nRich Pauloo's user avatar \n\nRich PaulooRich Pauloo \n\n8,47244 gold badges4141 silver badges7676 bronze badges \n\nAdd a comment  | \n\n3 \n\n**Edit: This approach is not secure. I was using it on a dummy-dev project. See explanation from Sun (in the reply) and check Peter Evan's answer**\n\nHowever, in my case, none of the answers worked. Here's how I fixed it.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n---\nname: Build and Push Docker Image to AWS ECR\non:\n  push:\n    branches: [ master ]\n\nenv:\n  FOO: '${{ secrets.FOO }}'\n\njobs:\n  build-and-push:\n    name: Build Project and Push to AWS ECR\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n\n    steps:\n      - name: Checkout\n        uses: actions/checkout@v2\n        \n        ... \n        \n      - name: Build and Push to AWS ECR\n        id: build-image\n        env:\n          ECR_REGISTRY: ${{ steps.login-ecr.outputs.registry }}\n        run: |\n          docker build --build-arg FOO=$FOO -t $ECR_REGISTRY/crew-charge-app:latest .\n          docker push $ECR_REGISTRY/crew-charge-app:latest\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nI first had to get the FOO variable from github secrets using ${{secrets.FOO}} then pass it onto the docker file using docker build --build-arg FOO=$FOO --build-arg BAR=$BAR -t .\n\nThen inside the docker file I had to declare both as an ARG and ENV to be available at all times.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nFROM node:14\n\nARG FOO=${FOO}\n\nENV FOO=${FOO}\n\nRUN mkdir -p /usr/src/app\n\nWORKDIR /usr/src/app\n\nCOPY package.json /usr/src/app\n\nRUN yarn install\n\nCOPY . /usr/src/app\n\nRUN FOO=$FOO yarn build\n\nEXPOSE 80\n\nCMD [\"yarn\", \"start\" ]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nImportant part was to RUN FOO=$FOO yarn build because setting the ENV alone doesn't pass it onto the container.\n\nShare \n\nImprove this answer \n\n Follow \n\nedited Jun 20, 2023 at 7:47 \n\n answered Mar 6, 2022 at 17:40 \n\nBharadwaj Giridhar's user avatar \n\nBharadwaj GiridharBharadwaj Giridhar \n\n1,2571414 silver badges1616 bronze badges \n\n2 \n\n* 5  \nNever do this. this is insecure in the case where FOO supposed to be secret value --build-arg FOO=$FOO means you will be able to see the cached secret when any user who has access to image can run the command docker history \u003cimagename\u003e  \n– Sun  \nCommented Oct 4, 2022 at 12:23\n* I presume this is perfectly safe in cases where FOO is not an important value?  \n– C.
